long_biography.plain_text:
Shipowner Bertram Rickmers bought back the former family business Rickmers-Linie from Hapag-Lloyd in 2000. Under his ownership, it developed a regular global service for heavy machinery and other oversized cargo. Ships followed a fixed eastbound circuit, with departures every fortnight, allowing customers to plan deliveries for large industrial projects. Adjustable decks and powerful onboard cranes helped accommodate unusual loads.

Expansion also depended on financial arrangements that pooled private investors' money in individual ships and added bank borrowing. The shipping downturn exposed the risks of this model. Rickmers Holding struggled with expensive debt and entered insolvency in 2017, after its heavy-lift division had been sold.

confidence.reason: Primary annual report explains service design; contemporary maritime reporting supports equipment, and trade obituary plus public-broadcaster history support financing and insolvency sequence.
